scope: Independent read-only logic review of actual draft sources; no implementation changes, no fixture reruns, no external writes or runner execution.
conclusion: No deterministic first-run blocker or silent omission of baseline manifest payload identified, assuming final six overlay measurements and approved workflow-only pre-apply change.

findings.severity: bounded robustness gap, not observed failure
findings.location: publish-edition19.yml final release edit command and upload/download-by-tag commands
findings.issue: The draft release is initially bound by numeric ID and later verified by ID, but gh release upload/download/edit resolve it again by tag. Successful final verification still requires the original ID. Thus no silent wrong-release success was found, but the final write itself does not carry the pinned ID.
findings.minimal_change: Replace only final gh release edit with gh api --method PATCH repos/$EXPECTED_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_RELEASE_ID --field draft=false --raw-field target_commitish=$PUBLISH_COMMIT_SHA, retaining all existing post-verification. For upload/download, optionally require exactly one tag match across all release states before the operation; no need to rewrite the pipeline for an unobserved duplicate.

findings.severity: history packaging precondition, resolved in observed workspace
findings.issue: Old mutable root docs are allowed to change; preservation in the downloadable archive relies on explicit snapshots. Git history alone is not part of a payload-only ZIP.
findings.observed: All three root snapshots and REPOSITORY_MANIFEST snapshot now exist and match the baseline exactly. They must be included in the new manifest and overlay.
findings.status: Verified actual files; final manifest inclusion pending root freeze

findings.location: applier --verify-only vs actual apply; runner strict gate
findings.issue: verify-only validates reconstructed listed bytes but does not execute Git ancestry/dirty-check or baseline subset preservation gate. Those gates run in actual apply.
findings.observed: Workflow calls real apply followed by verify_repository.py --strict; no local limited verification can replace these steps.
findings.status: No change needed; accurately limit local claims

findings.location: baseline diff guard; draft query; remote_tag_target; existing-asset cmp
findings.issue: Unexpected main changes, a published release instead of draft, an existing tag targeting a different commit, or an incomplete/different existing asset stop the job. They are not auto-overwritten.
findings.minimal_change: No relaxation recommended. Do not create actual v19 tag before the job; do not add other remote payload commits before application. Inspect observed asset failures before any targeted repair.

invariant_checks: First gate rejects unfilled SHA/count/size/part placeholders before network.
Exact named 32MiB ordered parts are selected by asset ID, size-checked and combined; ZIP SHA verified before executing its applier.
Fresh apply requires fixed baseline ancestor, only publish-edition19.yml changed from baseline, and clean checkout.
New applier and packager agree on six exact metadata names; metadata and manifest cannot be payload rows.
Actual apply preserves every baseline payload row except approved mutable root docs; added paths are restricted.
Runner full checkout, full byte validation and strict-extra-file check precede commit.
Commit uses only manifest literal paths plus manifest and new receipt. Branch push is not forced.
Packager includes every manifest payload plus manifest and all six metadata in full ZIP, verifies CRC and each member hash; current project ZIP uses only current/EGA_v19.
Eight output filenames agree between packager and workflow; no clobber flag; existing bytes must match.
Every expected uploaded asset is uniquely found by name in pinned release ID, size/state and SHA256 or downloaded cmp verified.
Tag is created only if absent, otherwise must already resolve to final commit; annotated dereference supported; post-publication tag and release ID rechecked.

official_references.supports: Upload interface is tag-based; clobber deletes before reupload.
Edit interface is tag-based; draft=false publication and target option.
Update endpoint is PATCH by numeric release_id; draft false publishes; target differing in workflows from default branch may require extra workflow authorization.
Asset binary retrieval via asset ID with Accept application/octet-stream; SHA256 digest metadata.

permissions_reasoning: Workflow pushes verified commit to main before release update. In this intended state target is default-branch commit, so no workflow-file difference relative to default branch is introduced by release update. Current runner write ability was not probed by this reviewer.
limitations: No real overlay or final new manifest available to this review
No GitHub write or runner execution
No proof that a future network upload succeeds
No full local historic payload checkout
